## Comparability check

All five companies report on a calendar fiscal year (Jan 1 – Dec 31) for both FY2023 and FY2024, so the periods line up directly [DOC-1]. One caveat: the excerpt provides only as‑reported revenue and operating income and does not disclose whether any of the year‑over‑year changes reflect acquisitions, divestitures, or segment redefinitions. Alaska's outsized growth in particular should be read as an as‑reported figure that may include inorganic contributions, which the source does not break out. Also note that "strongest performer" is metric‑dependent, so I show the main scorecards below.

## FY2024 scorecard

| Airline | FY2024 Revenue | FY2024 Op. income | Op. margin FY24 | Op. margin FY23 | Rev. growth | Op. income growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta [DOC-1] | $61,643M | $5,995M | 9.7% | 9.5% | +6.2% | +8.6% |
| United [DOC-1] | $57,063M | $5,096M | 8.9% | 7.8% | +6.2% | +21.0% |
| Southwest [DOC-1] | $27,483M | $321M | 1.2% | 0.9% | +5.3% | +43.3% |
| American [DOC-1] | $54,211M | $2,614M | 4.8% | 5.7% | +2.7% | −13.8% |
| Alaska [DOC-1] | $11,735M | $570M | 4.9% | 3.8% | +12.6% | +44.7% |

Supporting figures: Delta "Revenue FY2023 $58,048M, FY2024 $61,643M. Operating income FY2023 $5,521M, FY2024 $5,995M" [DOC-1]; United "Revenue FY2023 $53,717M, FY2024 $57,063M. Operating income FY2023 $4,211M, FY2024 $5,096M" [DOC-1]; Southwest "Revenue FY2023 $26,091M, FY2024 $27,483M. Operating income FY2023 $224M, FY2024 $321M" [DOC-1]; American "Revenue FY2023 $52,788M, FY2024 $54,211M. Operating income FY2023 $3,034M, FY2024 $2,614M" [DOC-1]; Alaska "Revenue FY2023 $10,426M, FY2024 $11,735M. Operating income FY2023 $394M, FY2024 $570M" [DOC-1].

## Interpretation

- **Delta** is the strongest on the measures that matter most for absolute earning power: the highest operating margin of the group (9.7%) and the largest operating income ($5,995M), achieved on the largest revenue base ($61,643M), with margin still expanding year over year [DOC-1].
- **United** is the closest challenger and arguably the best "improvement" story among the large carriers: +21.0% operating income growth and roughly 110 bps of margin expansion, though its 8.9% margin still trails Delta [DOC-1].
- **Alaska** posts the fastest growth rates (+12.6% revenue, +44.7% operating income), but from a far smaller base and at a 4.9% margin — roughly half Delta's [DOC-1]; as noted, the source does not isolate any inorganic contribution.
- **Southwest** shows large percentage income growth off a near‑breakeven base, but a 1.2% operating margin is the weakest economics in the group [DOC-1].
- **American** is the clear laggard: the slowest revenue growth (+2.7%), the only decline in operating income (−13.8%), and margin compression of about 90 bps [DOC-1].

If "strongest performer" were defined purely as year‑over‑year momentum, the answer would be Alaska (or United among the large carriers). On the balance of scale, absolute profit, and margin, Delta leads.

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines — it posted the highest FY2024 operating margin (9.7%) and the largest operating income ($5,995M) on the largest revenue base ($61,643M), with margins still expanding; United was the runner‑up and the fastest‑improving large carrier (+21.0% operating income), while American was the clear laggard (the only operating income decline, −13.8%).
